0.x: **Hathigumpha inscription** (2nd–1st c. BCE): the year-by-year record of **Kharavela** of Kalinga.
**Udayagiri and Khandagiri:** Both natural and artificial caves; **Udayagiri 18, Khandagiri 15** caves.
**Religion:** A **Jaina** – the king who "heavily leaned towards Jainism"; gave caves to Jain monks; brought back from Magadha the **Jina image** taken by the Nandas.
**Campaigns:** Sent an army west **ignoring Satakarni**; raided Magadha; southern victories; canal work begun by a Nanda king.
**Other pairs:** Nasik – Gautami Balashri; **Nanaghat – Naganika**; Junagadh – Rudradaman.

1.x: **Brihadratha**, the last Maurya and **7th king after Ashoka**, was killed by his **senani Pushyamitra Sunga** at an **army review** – a military coup.

r: **Immediate successors of the Mauryas in Magadha**; dynasty founded **187 BC**
**Succeeded the Mauryas in the Deccan**; earlier Mauryan feudatories; founder **Simuka (Srimukha)**; the Puranas call them **Andhra-bhrityas**
**Vasudeva Kanva** killed the last Sunga **Devabhuti**; **four** kings (c. 73–28 BC); the last, **Susharman**, fell to the **Satavahanas**

1.x: **Pushyamitra:** Brahmana of the **Bharadvaja gotra**, **Senapati**; two Ashvamedhas (**Ayodhya inscription of Dhanadeva**); **Malavikagnimitram** – grandson **Vasumitra** beat a Yavana army on the Sindhu.
**Persecution debate:** the Divyavadana calls Pushyamitra a persecutor, yet **Sanchi and Bharhut** grew under the Sungas.

r: Pro-Buddhist policy and ban on sacrifices angered Brahmins; the Sungas and Kanvas were Brahmins
Non-violence after Kalinga dulled the army
Army, bureaucracy and gifts to the Sangha emptied the treasury; heavy taxes even on actors and prostitutes
Rule depended on the king; weak successors
Revolts at Taxila against wicked officials

2.x: **Financial-crisis evidence:** spending on **Dhamma missions** and the **Sangha**; **debasement of later punch-marked silver coins**; gold images melted.
**Other factors:** spread of iron and material culture to outlying areas; neglect of the **north-west frontier** while China built the Great Wall (c. 220 BC).

3.x: **Later Mauryas:** Kunala, Dasharatha, **Samprati** (Jain patron), Shalishuka, Devavarman, Shatadhanvan, **Brihadratha** – the Vishnu Purana lists seven successors.

r: **Kunala, later Samprati**; Indo-Greeks supplanted it by **180 BC**
Diverted Scythian tribes westward and southward towards India

3.x: **Menander = Milinda**; capital **Sagala (Sialkot)**; dialogue with **Nagasena** in the Milindapanha.
There was no permanent alliance with the Indo-Greeks.
